lens: COMPARISON VALIDITY (ICAPS reviewer): would the TAMPURA-vs-ours numbers from P4.6, with decisions D3/D8/D9, be accepted as a fair same-task comparison?

findings.title: D3 scores holding with a PyBullet body id; TAMPURA's reward needs the store symbol, so every O episode would score 0
findings.problem: D3 says 'grasp_body = the contacted body's id (never the target's name)'. TAMPURA's abstract belief emits Atom('holding', [self.grasp_body]) verbatim and the reward's Exists substitutes store symbols from type_dict['physical'] (strings like 'o_ph_3') into Atom('holding', ['?o']) and tests Atom equality. Their own pick_execute_fn sets obs.grasp_body = obj, the store SYMBOL, not store.get(obj). A raw integer body id never equals a symbol, so rewards[-1] == 1.0 is unreachable for our arm and G12 would report 0/20 regardless of what the robot did. The plan also leaves 'grasp' unspecified although Belief.update only copies grasp_body when observation.grasp is not None.
findings.evidence: env.py:309-311 (Atom('holding', [self.grasp_body])); env.py:393-394 (obs.grasp = grasp symbol, obs.grasp_body = obj symbol); env.py:297-302 (grasp_body copied only if observation.grasp is not None); symbolic.py:382-404 (Exists iterates type_dict[t] and compares Atom equality); env.py:70-73 (their id-to-symbol lookup: store.get(obj_sym) == body); plan line 'grasp_body = the contacted body's id (never the target's name)'
findings.required_change: Rewrite D3: grasp_body = the store symbol s with store.get(s) == the body id both finger pads contact (the same lookup obs_from_camera_image uses, env.py:70-73); grasp = a symbol of type 'grasp' added once via store.add_typed(our grasp pose, 'grasp') so at-grasp(o, g) is well formed; if the contacted body maps to no physical symbol (table, robot) grasp stays None. Add two G6 pytest cases: a verified squeeze on the die body yields problem_spec.get_reward == 1.0 with conf = DEFAULT_ARM_POS; the same squeeze on a cup body yields 0.0. The symbol lookup is a readback-to-name mapping, not an oracle, and must be documented as the ONLY store read in scoring.

findings.title: at-home: G6 forbids the constant, B7/R3 contemplate a 'tolerance rule'; the two cannot both hold, and our executor converges to 2e-3 rad against their 1e-4
findings.problem: TAMPURA's at-home is np.allclose(conf, DEFAULT_ARM_POS, rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-4), i.e. about 1e-4 to 3.7e-4 rad per joint. Our move executor's endpoint hold stops at max joint error < 2e-3 rad after at most 120 steps. Under position control with gravity and a payload the readback will routinely sit between 1e-4 and 2e-3, so with D3's 'conf = the real joint readback' the strict count could be near 0/20 for a numerical reason, not a method reason. B7 then says 'pre-register in BF# the tolerance rule the campaign uses and report the strict count alongside', but a tolerance rule can only be realised by writing a conf that is not the readback (forbidden by G6: 'never the DEFAULT_ARM_POS constant') or by editing their at-home (forbidden by H4). The plan therefore has no admissible remedy written down and discovers the problem at B7, after B2-B6.
findings.evidence: env.py:318-321 (allclose rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-4); robot_utils.py:777-788 (hold loop: break when max |q - target| < 2e-3, 120 steps cap, force=240); plan G6 'joint readback for conf, never the DEFAULT_ARM_POS constant'; plan B7 'pre-register in BF# the tolerance rule the campaign uses'
findings.required_change: Strike the tolerance rule from B7. State that the only admissible remedies are executor-side and general: (a) the endpoint hold of a move whose target is a declared sensing/goal configuration runs until max joint error < 1e-4 rad or a bounded step cap, as a main-pipeline change A/B'd on our scenes (B3 style) or as a G9 executor parameter derived from the task spec's goal tolerance, counted inside loop time; or (b) honest failure. Move the measurement to B1: on OUR table, drive the Panda to DEFAULT_ARM_POS holding a 5 g body under gravity and record the converged max joint error and the steps needed; the decision is recorded before B2. Add a secondary column for O: episodes where their belief holds holding(die) but not at-home, so the reader sees the strictness cost.

findings.title: The pinch-span gate decides all three layouts, not 'two of three': every scene hides the die under a d or e cup
findings.problem: R1 says a span failure yields 'honest failures on two of three layouts'. In the scene files the die is at d_cups_ud's point in 1747173591, at e_cups_ud's point in 1747173593, and 1.5 cm from d_cups_ud in 1747173590; d and e are the two largest of the five cup classes shipped (JSON z of d 0.0493 and e 0.0523 vs a 0.0448, b 0.0459, with z = stable z + 0.01, so d is about 7.9 cm and e about 8.5 cm tall and correspondingly wider at the rim). If the d or e class AABB width exceeds GRASP_MAX_SPAN = 0.076 (our sampler takes the pinch width from the AABB, i.e. the rim of an inverted cup), our arm cannot uncover the die in ANY seed and the campaign is 0/20 by construction. That is a measurement of the grasp sampler, not of the representation or the planner, and the paper could not attribute the result. B6 currently allows this outcome to be run as 'honest'.
findings.evidence: problems/1747173590.312597.json (dice (0.592,-0.242) vs d_cups_ud (0.588,-0.228)); problems/1747173591.670785.json ([d_cups_ud, dice] at the same point); problems/1747173593.826745.json (dice at e_cups_ud's point (0.486,-0.158)); env_generator.py:117 (z = stable_z + 0.01); streams.py:719 (GRASP_MAX_SPAN = 0.076); plan R1 'honest failures on two of three layouts'
findings.required_change: Correct R1 to 'all three layouts'. In B1 measure, per cup class, the collision-mesh AABB width AND the top-face (inverted base) width, and the Panda URDF finger limits. B6 then records one of two pre-registered outcomes BEFORE B7: (i) d and e fit the span as the sampler stands, no change; (ii) they do not, and the general top-face pinch-width refinement is adopted with its own BF# entry and an A/B on our scenes, or the campaign is declared not runnable and the user decides. Add an exit reason 'no_grasp_in_span' (stream offered no grasp for a may_cover object the plan needed) so that any such failure is attributable in the taxonomy. A campaign whose outcome is fixed before it runs is not a measurement and must not be quoted as one.

findings.title: The significance rule is wrong for n = 20: a 3-seed difference is noise and even a 6-seed difference is not significant; the paired structure is unused
findings.plan_location: P4.6 REPETITIONS AND NOISE, RESULT TABLE
findings.problem: 'Differences under 3 seeds in 20 are reported as not significant' implies that 3 or more might be. With 20 vs 20 episodes, 11/20 vs 14/20 gives Fisher two-sided p about 0.5 and 11/20 vs 17/20 about 0.08; only a landslide of roughly 7 or more seeds reaches p < 0.05. The plan also does not say which repetition is the headline, whether the two blocks are pooled to n = 40 (they must not be: the same three layouts and the same seeds), and it ignores that the design is PAIRED (same seed, same scene file on both arms), where a per-seed discordance table and McNemar's exact test are the natural, more powerful primary analysis. Without this, 'who did better' will be answered from a 2 or 3 seed gap that the plan's own noise floor (+/-1-2 seeds for identical code) explains.
findings.evidence: plan line 'differences under 3 seeds in 20 are reported as not significant'; PAPER_AUDIT.txt:2512-2522 (identical code flips 1-2 seeds per 20); map_eval.json (six same-quality configs spread 11 to 17 of 20); tampura_sweep.py:51-61 (aggregates are means only)
findings.required_change: Pre-register in P4.6: primary evidence = the paired per-seed table (seed, scene file, T outcome, O outcome, both times) for repetition 1; McNemar exact test on discordant seeds as the primary test, Fisher exact two-sided as secondary, Wilson 95 % on each rate; a sentence stating that at n = 20 only differences of about 7 seeds or more reach p < 0.05, so the headline is descriptive with intervals; repetition 2 is the stability check (flips reported), never pooled; the 3-seed figure is called the noise floor, not a significance threshold. Per-layout rates (8, 7, 5 seeds) are reported without tests.

findings.title: Time comparison: T's loop time is computation only (headless teleport, no physics), O's adds stepped physics; no symmetric planning-only number exists for T, and the 20-step vs 900 s asymmetry is footnoted instead of shown
findings.problem: t1 (time_deltas[-1]) on T contains outcome sampling, SymK, IK/BiRRT and a teleport; execution costs no simulation time. On O it contains PDDLStream plus every physics step of every motion. t5 (planning only) is O-only by the plan's choice, so the one like-for-like quantity (planning share vs planning share) is never produced, although a wrapper in OUR code (a Policy subclass registered under a new name that times TampuraPolicy.get_action, and/or env.step timed from the driver) would give T's get_action vs env.step split without touching their tree. Separately, T's budget is 20 steps (failures end at 212 to 729 s in the baseline) while O's is 900 s of wall clock; the all-episode time means are therefore shaped by the budgets, not the methods, and a table footnote does not let the reader undo that. Finally, a killed episode has loop_s None and tampura_sweep.py's summarize() silently drops None, so all-episode time means on either arm would omit exactly the slowest episodes.
findings.evidence: policy.py:104-136 (time_deltas covers get_action + env.step + update); map_tampura.json/map_eval.json (panda_env_utils.py:928 teleport when no GUI, verified by the reader agents); tampura_sweep.py:51-53 (summarize drops None), 173 (loop_s None on kill); plan '(t5) planning-only time for O (sum of plan() spans), labelled O-only'; plan D9 'no action cap on our arm (their 20-step cap is their step semantics)'
findings.required_change: (a) Add to the T driver a timing wrapper in our code: a TampuraPolicy subclass registered as 'tampura_policy_timed' that records perf_counter around super().get_action, and env.step timed in the same subclass's rollout or by differencing; record it under G13 as the second runtime registration (or, if rejected, state in P4.6 that no planning-only comparison is made and delete t5 from the paper table). (b) Add an anytime figure: cumulative success fraction vs elapsed loop time up to 900 s for both arms (T: time_deltas at solve_step; O: time of the final action), which makes the step-cap vs wall-cap asymmetry visible and lets a reader pick any budget. (c) State that killed or crashed episodes enter all-episode time statistics at the cap value, flagged censored, on both arms. (d) Keep t1 headless on both arms but label T's as 'no physical simulation time'.

findings.title: D8's condition 'if their task bodies are static' misreads TAMPURA's objects: create_ycb passes baseMass = -1, which is neither static nor a usable dynamic mass
findings.problem: Every YCB body is created with createMultiBody(baseMass=-1). A readback of -1 is not 'static (mass 0)', so D8's trigger ('if their task bodies are static, they are made dynamic ONCE') may not fire, and stepping physics with a negative base mass gives an undefined contact response (negative inverse mass) for the die and every cup. The disclosure the paper would carry ('objects were static and were given masses') would then be false, and the settle itself (cups start 1 cm above the table by construction, the die 3 cm above it in two files) would be unrecorded in magnitude.
findings.evidence: panda_env_utils.py:676-702 (def create_ycb(..., mass=-1) -> client.createMultiBody(baseMass=mass, ...)); pb_utils.py:766, 823 (STATIC_MASS default only for table and primitives); env_generator.py:117 (z = stable_z_on_aabb + 0.01 for every object); plan D8 'if their task bodies are static (B1 verifies the masses), they are made dynamic ONCE'
findings.required_change: Rewrite D8: before the first physics step, every task body whose getDynamicsInfo mass is not strictly positive receives the declared class mass (die and cup masses from the task spec, cited to YCB) via one changeDynamics call, allowlisted under G1 and recorded in BF#; B1(c) records the raw readback (-1 expected). Log per episode the settle displacement of every task body (max XY and yaw drift between the JSON pose and the pose after the settle) and report the campaign maximum in the table notes, so 'same layouts' is a measured statement; state in the paper that in TAMPURA's own arm the bodies float 1 cm above the table for the whole episode.

findings.title: The scoring observation carries a ground-truth read (world.poses through obs_from_camera_image) that the reward never uses
findings.problem: The reward depends only on grasp_body (holding), the category table (is-target) and conf (at-home); observation.poses and camera_image only add known-pose atoms and a visibility update. Passing a real render through their obs_from_camera_image therefore pulls true poses of visible bodies into the scoring path for no scoring effect, and forces the G2 exception for the adapter to be wider than necessary (H1 letter: no ground-truth reads feeding success scoring).
findings.evidence: env.py:993-1004 (reward = Exists(is-target and holding) and at-home); env.py:285-302 (update: poses merged, visibility only if camera_image present, grasp copied); env.py:70-73 (obs_from_camera_image reads world.poses)
findings.required_change: D3: the terminal observation is SceneObservation(camera_image=None, poses={}, grasp=<grasp symbol or None>, grasp_body=<symbol or None>, conf=<readback>); G2's adapter exception shrinks to the store lookup and the contact/joint readback. If a camera image is wanted for the pickle, record it in our own ledger, not in their belief.

findings.title: t4 per-action time divides by incomparable action counts
findings.problem: A TAMPURA step is a macro action (pick = IK + BiRRT + approach + close + retreat; look = plan + move + render); our ledger counts move, pick, move, place, move, sense separately, so O's per-action time is mechanically 2 to 3 times smaller for the same work. A reviewer discards the column or reads it against us.
findings.evidence: plan '(t4) per-action time = loop time / actions executed (T: non-no-op steps; O: dispatched actions from the ledger)'; map_tampura.json pick_execute description (panda_env_utils.py:927-1034)
findings.required_change: Define O's count at macro level for t4 (pick, place, sense; each preceding move folded into the action it serves; the final move home folded into the goal), report the raw dispatched count beside it, or drop t4 and keep only 'actions to goal' with both definitions printed.

findings.title: M2's parity sentence overstates: TAMPURA's cavity is mesh-derived for any known object, ours is a declared class list
findings.plan_location: P4.5 M2 CLAIM EFFECT; P4.3 D5
findings.problem: 'Our class declaration is the same information TAMPURA takes from the known mesh' is not quite true: their visibility update keeps voxels that are not within 7.5 mm of ANY known object's collision mesh, with no per-class knowledge, so a bowl or a box would hide a die in their model without anyone declaring it; ours hides nothing under an object unless its category is in may_cover. The declaration is task knowledge TAMPURA computes geometrically. A reviewer will read the sentence as claiming equal information.
findings.evidence: env.py:142-238 (update_visibility, per map_tampura.json verified fact: voxels within GRID_RESOLUTION/2 of any known object's collision body are cleared); plan M2 'our class declaration is the same information TAMPURA takes from the known mesh'
findings.required_change: Word it as: 'a declared class property (hollow, may cover) stands in for TAMPURA's mesh-derived cavity test; theirs is geometric and generic over known meshes, ours is declared per class; the generic variant (cast an interior for every object) exists behind a task-spec switch and is not used because it changes the thesis scenes'. Keep this sentence in the paper's disclosures.

findings.title: G18 leaves it open whether our scene build runs inside their clock
findings.problem: T's analogue of our first render + boxelization + shadow casting + octree (flat stream sampling, 58 to 96 s at t = 0) runs inside get_action and so inside time_deltas. If the bridge builds the env_adapter in the policy constructor or in run_bridge_on_finddice.py before policy.rollout, that cost falls outside time_deltas on O only.
findings.evidence: policy.py:103-136 (clock starts before step 0; get_action and env.step inside); map_tampura.json (outcome sampling 58 s at t = 0 for seed 0 inside the loop); plan D2 'our execute_fn runs the entire plan-act-sense loop'
findings.required_change: Add to G18 and D2: 'between env.initialize() returning and the first env.step, the bridge performs only the schema registration; the env adapter, first render, boxelization and shadow casting happen inside execute_fn', and assert it with a ledger timestamp check in bridge_gates.

findings.title: Die detectability from home is feasible but the visibility thresholds differ (1 pixel for T, 6 localisable pixels for O); the plan does not measure it
findings.problem: Estimate: the die is about 2.2 cm (JSON z 0.0209 = stable z + 0.01). The home wrist camera must image x in [0.3,0.7], y in [-0.4,0.4] (generator rejects out-of-image poses) within a 62.7 x 49 degree FOV, so the die is 0.5 to 1.0 m away, i.e. 11 to 23 pixels across at fx 525, well above DETECTION_MIN_PIXELS = 6. Detection from home is therefore feasible in principle. But TAMPURA counts an object visible if its id appears in ANY pixel of the mask and then hands out its exact pose, while ours needs 6 pixels and a localisable depth cloud; a die peeking out 1 to 5 pixels from behind a cup after the settle is 'found' for T and not for O. B1(e) only asserts the die absent from the three home masks at the start; it does not measure the revealed die's pixel count.
findings.evidence: perception.py:320 (DETECTION_MIN_PIXELS = 6), perception.py:381-435 (min_pixels gate before unprojection); env.py:64-73 (np.unique over the mask, any pixel counts); env_generator.py:131-148 (pose must project into the home image); robot intrinsics 640x480 fx = fy = 525 (map_tampura.json, robot.py:120-125)
findings.required_change: B1(e): for each scene file, render the home view with each may_cover cup parked away in turn and record the die's pixel count and the AABB estimate error of our detector; add the 1-pixel vs 6-pixel visibility asymmetry to the table notes; if any revealed die renders under 6 pixels from home, that scene is a disclosed limitation of the fixed-eye choice (D4), not a reason to lower the gate.

findings.title: No claim ledger: the plan must say which thesis sentences the campaign measures and which stay architectural
findings.plan_location: P4.5 CLAIM EFFECT (M1-M4), P4.6 RESULT TABLE
findings.problem: The CLAIM EFFECT lines cover the model tweaks but not the comparison sentences the paper will inherit from the thesis. Without a ledger, the same indirect sentences (per-step 11 s vs 57 s, 'rough parity', 'comparable in reliability') can survive next to measured numbers.
findings.evidence: results.tex:295 (per-episode 144.4 vs 166 s; per-step 11 s vs 57 s; 'marginally easier goal'; 'benchmarks neither system'); results.tex:300 (figure caption); results.tex:352 (occlusion sub-symbolic, view-blind placement); results.tex:354 ('sufficient ... at comparable end-to-end cost and reliability, and simpler to model'); results.tex:389-404 ('not the same problem', hardware, 'shared scene file would strengthen'); conclusion.tex:27-45 (sensing configuration and concave interiors as future work)
findings.required_change: Add to P4.5 a CLAIM LEDGER. MEASURED by B8 (only if the blockers above are fixed): results.tex:295 per-episode time parity and :295/:300 reliability (replaced by same-task, same-machine, same-seed numbers with intervals); :295 'marginally easier goal' (deleted: D6 makes the goals identical); :354 'sufficient to reach the goal at comparable cost and reliability' (measured on find_dice only: one task, three layouts, 20 seeds, worded with that scope); :389-404 'not the same problem' and 'shared scene file would strengthen' (resolved; hardware sentence updated to the campaign CPU). STAY ARCHITECTURAL and must be worded so: :352 symbolic vs sub-symbolic occlusion and view-blind placement (unmeasured unless a view-blocking-placement count is added to both arms from logs, optional); :295 per-step 11 s vs 57 s (drop: step semantics differ, their per-step includes 200 effects_fn samples); :354 'simpler to model' (qualitative); related-work statements on LAO* and the learned MDP (source-verified, unchanged); all semantic-vs-uniform partition claims (ours-only, untouched by this campaign); M1 and M2 are extensions used in find_dice only and the paper says so in the sentence that introduces them (conclusion.tex:27-33, 41-45 name both as future work).

what_the_plan_gets_right: Success is judged for both arms by TAMPURA's own get_reward on TAMPURA's belief through their env.step and Belief.update, with no bridge-side RESULT line (G12, D2); this is the correct cure for CB#123.

Our arm runs as one schema action inside their rollout so time_deltas[-1] covers our whole episode (G18), and the harness never writes their belief fields directly (the archived belief_bridge pattern is explicitly rejected).

Seed-for-seed with the scene file pinned per seed and asserted on both arms (G19), results stratified by the three layouts, no re-rolls or re-runs outside pre-registered repetitions, both arms interleaved on the same idle machine, headless on both, find_dice.yml and both TAMPURA commits recorded.
The at-home strictness asymmetry is recognised and chosen as a disclosed virtue rather than imitated (D3), and go-home no_path is a failure for our arm.

The containment extension is a representation change (an interior region of the same type as a shadow, searched by the unchanged sense action) and the fixed eye is a planned move to a declared configuration, not an unplanned park (D4, D5, M1, M2), with the thesis's own future-work paragraphs cited.

Budgets are pre-registered (900 s wall on both arms, their 20 steps as shipped, our plan time bounded by the episode), action counts are reported on both arms, Wilson intervals are planned, times are reported all-episode and success-only, and TAMPURA's SymK seconds are never presented as planning time.

The disclosure list for the table notes (containment vs lateral shadows, wrist camera at home, kinematic vs physical execution, perfect poses vs depth estimates, grasp library vs contact grasp, settle and masses, three layouts) is the right inventory; it only needs the corrections above to be true in every item.
The gate set (G1-G19) names, for each gate, the archived violation it would have caught, and the fault-injection tests for scoring (G6) are the right kind of evidence for a reviewer.
